Do you wish, he says, that the earth be split, and that the underworld, which is said to be in the heart of the earth, lie open with a great gaping; or that the heavens be opened? Both of which pertain to the type of the Lord's death and ascension: For he who descended is the same who also ascended (Eph 4:10). And in the Apostle we read: Do not say in your heart, Who has ascended into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down. Or, Who has descended into the abyss? that is, to bring Christ back from the dead (Rom 10:6-7). And in another place, disputing about Christ, he says: What is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth of the surpassing knowledge and love of Christ (Eph 3:18). This, so far as concerns the mystical senses. But Moses too received signs from the earth, of which we read in the Psalms: He sent signs and wonders in the midst of you, O Egypt (Ps 134 [135]:9), frogs, locusts, gnats, and the dog-fly; and from heaven hail and fire and darkness of three days. I think that Hezekiah too, when the sun went back ten lines, received a sign from heaven (2 Kgs 20); and Joshua the son of Nun at Gibeon and Aijalon, when the sun and the moon stood still (Josh 10). Most think that Saul received a sign from the earth and from the depth of hell, when he seemed to have raised up Samuel through incantations and magic arts (1 Sam 28). But Jonah the prophet too, freed from the abyss, and from the deep and the jaws of death, gave and received the sign of hell (Jonah 2). I have read in the Commentaries of a certain man that this place was thinned out through allegory, so that he understood the depth and the height as αἰσθητὰ and νοητὰ, which we can call sensible things and intelligible things, of which the one is referred to the senses, the other to the mind and reason. The Virgin too he interprets as the soul which is corrupted by no consciousness of sin, and can bring forth from itself Emmanuel, God with us, that is, the present word of God. But we do not eat the flesh of the lamb boiled (Exod 12), but roasted, and such as can dry up in us all the phlegm of pleasures, lest, while we are wise beyond what we ought to be wise, we neglect the mystery of our faith.
Against Heresies (Book III, Chapter 21), Section 6

But what Isaiah said, "From the height above, or from the depth beneath," was meant to indicate, that "He who descended was the same also who ascended." But in this that he said, "The Lord Himself shall give you a sign," he declared an unlooked-for thing with regard to His generation, which could have been accomplished in no other way than by God the Lord of all, God Himself giving a sign in the house of David. For what great thing or what sign should have been in this, that a young woman conceiving by a man should bring forth,-a thing which happens to all women that produce offspring? But since an unlooked-for salvation was to be provided for men through the help of God, so also was the unlooked-for birth from a virgin accomplished; God giving this sign, but man not working it out.
HOMILIES ON ISAIAH 2

As far as the wording goes, Ahaz acted modestly when he had been commanded to "ask a sign in the depth or in the height"; and he gave a reason why he was unwilling to "ask," for he said: "I will not ask, nor will I tempt the Lord." And yet for this modesty he is blamed, and it is said to him: "Hear now, O house of David: is it a small thing for you to offer a contest to men, and how do you offer a contest to the Lord?" Then this promise is spoken: "Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, a virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel." Let these things be expounded, and as for the rest we shall look at them as we have need, and in those matters too the grace of God, that they may be made manifest. He is bidden to "ask a sign," not simply, but "for himself"; for the word says: "ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God in the depth or in the height." The "sign" set before him is "the Lord," my Jesus Christ. For this is the "sign" which he is bidden to "ask for himself in the depth or in the height." "In the depth" indeed, because "he who descended is the very same"; but "in the height," because "he who ascended above all the heavens is the very same." Yet to me this "sign" that is set before me, my "Lord" Jesus Christ, "in the depth and in the height," is of no profit, unless the mystery concerning his "depth" and "height" comes to be for me. For when I have received the mystery concerning Christ Jesus, concerning his "depth" and "height," then I shall receive the "sign" according to the commandment of the Lord, and it will be said to me, as to one having in himself "the depth and the height": "Say not in your heart: who shall ascend into heaven? — that is, to bring Christ down. Or who shall descend into the abyss? — that is, to bring Christ back from the dead. The word is near you, mighty in your mouth and in your heart." Therefore it is enjoined upon us all that we "ask" this "sign" for ourselves, that the "sign" which "the Lord God gives in the depth and in the height" may become useful to us. But if there is anyone who knows how to use reasonable contemplation, let him recognize this, that what is said, "in the depth and in the height," is not said disjunctively; for it signifies this, that he is able to be both. "Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord in the depth and in the height." And in the promise too the Apostle said: "that we may know what is the depth and the height and the breadth and the length." "And Ahaz says: I will not ask." He was unbelieving; for it was said: "ask for yourself." But the people even to this day does not "ask a sign," and therefore does not have him, and the people "offers a contest to the Lord" — the people that does not receive my Lord Jesus Christ. Then another question follows. For when this man says: "I will not ask, nor will I tempt the Lord," and reckons it to be a temptation if he "should ask a sign," it is said: "Hear now, O house of David: is it a small thing for you to offer a contest to men, and how do you offer a contest to the Lord?" But he does not "offer a contest to the Lord," nor do I think that he "offers a contest" even "to men," the one who "asks a sign in the depth or in the height." For the "contest" is God's, namely how he may save man. Therefore he does not "offer a contest to the Lord" who "takes refuge in salvation"; but he who, while the Lord contends to save man, flees from salvation and withdraws far from the Lord, "offers a contest to the Lord." "Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, a virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel." The true text of the copies of this prophet says: "you shall call." Moreover in Matthew we know it is read: "and they shall call his name Emmanuel." We cannot say that we ought to make anything less of the prophet. But how does the Gospel have this reading? Whether it was by someone who did not understand and ran to the easier course, as has happened also in many other places, or whether perhaps someone might say that the Gospel was published so from the beginning? Let him who wishes deliberate. The prophet indeed manifestly has: "and you shall call his name Emmanuel." I have known a certain man who, reading at the opening of the scriptures of the Gospel, "and you shall call his name Emmanuel," said within himself: 'What is "you shall call"? Who "shall call"? "Ahaz"; and how can "Ahaz" hear concerning the Savior, who came after many generations: "you shall call his name Emmanuel"?' and so, in place of what is, "you shall call," he wrote: "they shall call." But see that it is not to "Ahaz" that it is said: "and you shall call his name Emmanuel," but to the "house of David"; see that it is manifestly said: "Hear now, O house of David: is it a small thing for you to offer a contest to men, and how do you offer a contest to the Lord? Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, a virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel." If, therefore, at any time we do not understand what has been said, let us make nothing less of it nor run to the easier course, but let us wait for the grace of God to supply to us, through the illumination of knowledge, the explanation of the question — or else, again, let the grace of God, through whom it wills, illumine us, so that we may seek no further, but our question may be resolved; and if we are counted worthy of understanding from the Lord, he will the more readily plead our very cause. What, then, is the "house of David"? If "David" is Christ, as I have often proved, the "house of David" is we, the Church of God; and it is said to us who are the Church, that we should not "offer a contest to the Lord" as said above, but that, when the Lord gives a "sign," we should receive it. To us, not to the "house of David," are these things said. And it is prophesied that, if anyone is of the "house of David," he "shall call his name Emmanuel"; for at the coming of Christ our Church alone says of Christ: "God with us." These things having been explained, as the grace of the Lord has granted, let us now inquire into other riddles.
Commentary on Isaiah

And Ahaz said: I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord. It is not of humility but of pride that he will not ask a sign from the Lord. For although it is written in Deuteronomy: You shall not tempt the Lord your God (Deut 6:16), and the Savior used this testimony against the devil (Matt 4), yet, having been ordered to ask, he ought to have fulfilled the command by obedience, especially since both Gideon and Manoah asked for a sign and received it (Judg 6 and 13). And yet, according to the ambiguity of the Hebrew speech, in which is written ULO ENASSE ADONAI (ולא אנסה את יהוה), and all have likewise translated I will not tempt the Lord, it can be read I will not exalt the Lord. For the impious king knew that if he asked for a sign he would receive it, and the Lord would be glorified. So, as a worshipper of idols, who had set up altars at every corner of the streets and on the mountains and in the leafy groves, and had fanatics in place of Levites, he will not ask the sign that was commanded.
Against Heresies (Book III, Chapter 21), Section 5

And when He says, "Hear, O house of David," [Isaiah 7:13] He performed the part of one indicating that He whom God promised David that He would raise up from the fruit of his belly (ventris) an eternal King, is the same who was born of the Virgin, herself of the lineage of David. For on this account also, He promised that the King should be "of the fruit of his belly," which was the appropriate [term to use with respect] to a virgin conceiving, and not "of the fruit of his loins," nor "of the fruit of his reins," which expression is appropriate to a generating man, and a woman conceiving by a man. In this promise, therefore, the Scripture excluded all virile influence; yet it certainly is not mentioned that He who was born was not from the will of man. But it has fixed and established "the fruit of the belly," that it might declare the generation of Him who should be [born] from the Virgin, as Elisabeth testified when filled with the Holy Ghost, saying to Mary, "Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy belly;" [Luke 1:42] the Holy Ghost pointing out to those willing to hear, that the promise which God had made, of raising up a King from the fruit of [David's] belly, was fulfilled in the birth from the Virgin, that is, from Mary. Let those, therefore, who alter the passage of Isaiah thus, "Behold, a young woman shall conceive," and who will have Him to be Joseph's son, also alter the form of the promise which was given to David, when God promised him to raise up, from the fruit of his belly, the horn of Christ the King. But they did not understand, otherwise they would have presumed to alter even this passage also.
Commentary on Isaiah

And he said: Hear then, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to be troublesome to men, that you are troublesome to my God also? Who is this who said: Hear then, O house of David? Not at all God, who above had said to Ahaz: Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God; but the Prophet, as is proved from what follows: That you are troublesome to my God also. And the sense is: because you not only persecute the prophets and despise their sayings, but also contradict the sentence of God when he is present and commands; so that you cause labor to him who says in another place: I have labored in bearing it (Isa 1:14); for that reason the Lord will do the things that follow. For labor and trouble, which Aquila and Symmachus translated, the Seventy and Theodotion rendered agon, that is, wrestling and contest, because in their contentiousness they do not submit their neck to the service of the Lord, but, when he wishes to cure their wounds, spit out health. And this is to be noted, that when Ahaz, a most impious king, will not ask for a sign, the prophetic word is turned to the house of David, that is, to the royal tribe, of which we read above: And they told these things to the house of David, saying: Syria and Ephraim have come to an agreement.
The First Apology, Chapter XXXIII

And hear again how Isaiah in express words foretold that He should be born of a virgin; for he spoke thus: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bring forth a son, and they shall say for His name, `God with us.'" For things which were incredible and seemed impossible with men, these God predicted by the Spirit of prophecy as about to come to pass, in order that, when they came to pass, there might be no unbelief, but faith, because of their prediction. But lest some, not understanding the prophecy now cited, should charge us with the very things we have been laying to the charge of the poets who say that Jupiter went in to women through lust, let us try to explain the words. This, then, "Behold, a virgin shall conceive," signifies that a virgin should conceive without intercourse. For if she had had intercourse with any one whatever, she was no longer a virgin; but the power of God having come upon the virgin, overshadowed her, and caused her while yet a virgin to conceive. And the angel of God who was sent to the same virgin at that time brought her good news, saying, "Behold, thou shalt conceive of the Holy Ghost, and shalt bear a Son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest, and thou shalt call His name Jesus; for He shall save His people from their sins,"--as they who have recorded all that concerns our Saviour Jesus Christ have taught, whom we believed, since by Isaiah also, whom we have now adduced, the Spirit of prophecy declared that He should be born as we intimated before. It is wrong, therefore, to understand the Spirit and the power of God as anything else than the Word, who is also the first-born of God, as the foresaid prophet Moses declared; and it was this which, when it came upon the virgin and overshadowed her, caused her to conceive, not by intercourse, but by power. And the name Jesus in the Hebrew language means Saviour in the Greek tongue. Wherefore, too, the angel said to the virgin, "Thou shalt call His name Jesus, for He shall save His people from their sins." And that the prophets are inspired by no other than the Divine Word, even you, as I fancy, will grant.
Dialogue with Trypho, Chapter LXXXIV

Moreover, the prophecy, "Behold, the virgin shall conceive, and bear a son," was uttered respecting Him. For if He to whom Isaiah referred was not to be begotten of a virgin, of whom did the Holy Spirit declare, "Behold, the Lord Himself shall give us a sign: behold, the virgin shall conceive, and bear a son?" For if He also were to be begotten of sexual intercourse, like all other first-born sons, why did God say that He would give a sign which is not common to all the first-born sons? But that which is truly a sign, and which was to be made trustworthy to mankind,--namely, that the first-begotten of all creation should become incarnate by the Virgin's womb, and be a child,--this he anticipated by the Spirit of prophecy, and predicted it, as I have repeated to you, in various ways.
ON THE FLESH OF CHRIST 17

What is the sign? "Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son." In fact, a virgin did conceive and gave birth to "Emmanuel, God with us." This is the new birth: a man born from God. God was born in the man, taking the flesh of the old human race without the help of the old human seed. God took the flesh in order to reform the old human race with a new seed. In other words, he spiritually cleansed the old human race by removing its old stains.
LETTER 60:6
But what does this passage mean, if not that God has come in the flesh?
HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 5:3

And what goes before also establishes this interpretation. For he doth not merely say, "Behold, the Virgin shall be with child," but having first said, "Behold, the Lord Himself shall give you a sign," then he subjoins, "Behold, the Virgin shall be with child." Whereas, if she that was to give birth was not a virgin, but this happened in the way of marriage, what sort of sign would the event be? For that which is a sign must of course be beyond the course of common events, it must be strange and extraordinary; else how could it be a sign?
Against Jovinianus 1.32

Isaiah tells of the mystery of our faith and hope: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Emmanuel." I know that the Jews are accustomed to meet us with the objection that in Hebrew the word almah does not mean a virgin but "a young woman." And, to speak truth, a virgin is properly called bethulah, but a young woman, or a girl, is not almah but naarah! What then is the meaning of almah? A hidden virgin, that is, not merely virgin, but a virgin and something more, because not every virgin is hidden, shut off from the occasional sight of men.
Commentary on Isaiah

Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, a Virgin shall conceive and bear, and you shall call his name Emmanuel. No longer at sundry times, according to the apostle Paul, and in many ways will God speak (Heb 1); nor, according to another prophet (Hos 12), will he be likened in the hands of the prophets; but he who formerly spoke through others will himself say, I am here (below, 58). Of whom the Bride too was asking in the Song of Songs: Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth (Song 1:2). For the Lord of powers is himself the king of glory (Ps 23 [24]:10): he himself will descend into the virginal womb, and will enter and go out by the Eastern gate which is always shut (Ezek 44); of which Gabriel says to the Virgin: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you: therefore the holy thing that will be born in you will be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). And in Proverbs: Wisdom has built herself a house (Prov 9:1). And when it is said: The Lord himself will give you a sign, it ought to be new and marvelous. But if a young woman or a girl, as the Jews would have it, and not a virgin, gives birth, what sort of sign can it be called, since this is a name of age, not of integrity? And in truth, to set foot to foot with the Jews and not at all, with a contentious rope, give them occasion to laugh at our lack of skill: a virgin is called in Hebrew BETHULA (בתולה), which is not written in the present place; but in place of this word is set ALMA (עלמה), which all except the Seventy translated young girl. Now ALMA is an ambiguous word among them: for it is said both of a young girl and of one hidden, that is, ἀπόκρυφος..... Hence also in the title of the ninth psalm, where in the Hebrew is set ALAMOTH (עלמות), the other Translators translated for youth, what the Seventy rendered for the hidden things. And in Genesis we read, where Rebecca is called alma (Gen 24), that Aquila translated neither young girl nor girl but hidden. The Shunammite woman too, having lost her son, when she had thrown herself at the feet of Elisha and Gehazi was keeping her back, hears from the Prophet: Let her be, for she is in grief, and the Lord has hidden it from me (2 Kgs 4:27). In place of what is said in Latin, has hidden it from me, in the Hebrew is written EELIM MEMMENNI (העלים ממני). So alma is said not only of a girl or a virgin, but, with ἐπιτάσει, of a hidden virgin and a secluded one, who has never been open to the gaze of men, but has been guarded with great diligence by her parents. In the Punic tongue too, which is said to flow from the fountains of the Hebrews, a virgin is properly called alma. And, though we may give the Jews something to laugh at, in our own speech too alma means holy. And the Hebrews use words of almost all languages: as in the Song of Songs (Song 3:9), from the Greek φορεῖον, that is, litter, Solomon made himself one, which we also read thus in the Hebrew. The words nugas (trifles) and mensuram (measure) too the Hebrews call in the same way and with the same senses. And as far as I can contend with my memory, I think I have never read alma of a married woman, but of one who is a virgin: so that she is not only a virgin, but a virgin of younger age, and in the years of girlhood. For it can happen that a virgin is an old woman, but this virgin was in the years of girlhood. Or certainly a virgin, not a little girl and one who could not yet know a man, but now marriageable. Indeed, in Deuteronomy (Deut 22:25ff.) under the name of a girl and of a young woman a virgin is understood. If, he says, a man finds in the field a betrothed girl, and, overpowering her by force, lies with her, you shall kill only the man who lay with her, and to the girl you shall do nothing: the young woman has no sin worthy of death. For as when someone rises up in ambush against his neighbor and kills his life, so this matter happened. He found her in the field: the betrothed girl cried out, and there was none found to help her. And in the volume of Kings we read (1 Kgs 1) that they sought a girl, a virgin, named Abishag, and brought her in to the king, to sleep with him and to warm him; and the girl was exceedingly beautiful, and she ministered to him, and the king did not know her. And what follows: And you shall call his name Emmanuel, both the Seventy and the three others translated likewise, in place of which in Matthew is written they shall call: which is not found in the Hebrew. So this child who will be born of the Virgin, O house of David, let him now be called by you Emmanuel, that is, God with us, because by the very facts, being freed from two enemy kings, you will prove that you have God present; and he who will afterward be called Jesus, that is, Savior, because he is to save the whole race of men, let him now be called by you by the name of Emmanuel. The word CARATHI (קראת), which all have interpreted you shall call, can also be understood as she shall call: namely, that the Virgin herself, who will conceive and bear, is going to call Christ by this name. In many testimonies which the Evangelists or Apostles have taken from the old books, we must attend more carefully to the fact that they followed not the order of the words but the sense. Hence also in the present place, for shall conceive in the womb, Matthew set shall have in the womb (Matt 1:23); and for you shall call, they shall call. The Hebrews think that this is prophesied of Hezekiah the son of Ahaz, because in his reign Samaria was taken: which cannot be proved at all. Since Ahaz the son of Jotham reigned over Judah and Jerusalem sixteen years (2 Kgs 16), and his son Hezekiah succeeded him in the kingdom at twenty-five years of age, and reigned over Judah and Jerusalem twenty-nine years. How then, granting that this prophecy was made to Ahaz in his first year, is it said of the conception and birth of Hezekiah, when at the time Ahaz began to reign Hezekiah was already nine years old? Unless perhaps they say that the sixth year of Hezekiah's reign, in which Samaria was taken, is called his infancy, not of age but of rule. That this is forced and violent is plain even to fools. A certain one of our people contends that the prophet Isaiah had two sons, Jasub and Emmanuel, and that Emmanuel was begotten of the prophetess his wife, as a type of the Lord and Savior: so that the first son, Jasub, which is interpreted left or returning, signifies the Jewish people, which has been left and will afterward return; but the second, that is, Emmanuel, and God with us, the calling of the nations, after the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.
Commentary on Matthew

Now all this was done that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: Behold, a virgin shall have in the womb and shall bear. Where the evangelist Matthew says: shall have in the womb, in the prophet it is written: shall receive in the womb. But the prophet, because he foretells things to come, signifies what is to be and writes shall receive; the evangelist, because he narrates history not of the future but of the past, changed shall receive and put shall have. For one who has is by no means going to receive. Something of the kind we read in the psalms too: Ascending on high he led captivity captive, he received gifts among men. The Apostle, setting down this testimony, did not say received, but gave, because there it was signified of the future that he would receive, here it is told of him who had already given what he had received.
City of God 18.46

Christ was born a visible man of a human virgin mother, but he was a hidden God because God was his Father. So the prophet had foretold: "Behold, the virgin shall be with child and shall bring forth a son; and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which is interpreted, God with us." To prove that he was God, Christ worked many miracles, some of which—as many as seemed necessary to establish his claim—are recorded in the Gospels. Of these miracles the very first was the marvelous manner of his birth; the very last, his ascension into heaven in his body risen from the dead.
SERMON 370:3

You must appreciate, brothers and sisters, what a tremendous desire possessed the saints of old to see the Christ. They knew he was going to come, and all those who were living devout and blameless lives would say, "Oh, if only that birth may find me still here! Oh, if only I may see with my own eyes what I believe from God's Scriptures!" The saints who knew from the holy Scripture that a virgin was going to give birth as you heard when Isaiah was read: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb and shall bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel." What Emmanuel means the Gospel declares to us, saying, "which is interpreted, God with us." So do not let it surprise you, unbelieving soul, whoever you are, do not let it strike you as impossible that a virgin should give birth, and in giving birth remain a virgin. Realize that it was God who was born, and you will not be surprised at a virgin giving birth. So then, to prove to you how the saints and just men and women of old longed to see what was granted to this old man Simeon, our Lord Jesus Christ said, when speaking to his disciples, "Many just men and prophets have wished to see what you see and have not seen it; and to hear what you hear and have not heard it."
Homilies on the Gospels 1:5

The Savior's name, because of which he is called "God with us" by the prophet, signifies both natures of his one person. For he who, born before time from the Father, is God himself in the fullness of time, became Emmanuel (that is, "God with us") in his mother's womb, because he deigned to take the weakness of our nature into the unity of his person when "the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us." In a wonderful manner he began to be what we are, while not ceasing to be what he had been, assuming our nature in such a way that he himself would not lose what he had been.
HOMILIES ON ISAIAH 2

"Butter and honey shall he eat." How is it prophesied that Christ "shall eat butter and honey"? And even if this be expounded by the Lord's bestowing it, again the things that follow will press upon us other questions. And would that we all did that which is written: "Search the scriptures." Many things drawn from bodily foods are named in the scriptures for spiritual nourishment. "As newborn babes, desire the reasonable milk that is without guile." Therefore there is without doubt a "reasonable milk," and we ought to seek such "milk." Again, in Proverbs it is written concerning "honey": "finding honey, eat what is enough, lest perchance being full you vomit it up." And did the Holy Spirit take care about that "honey" which is commonly known, "lest perchance" we "eat" too much? But the Holy Spirit, surely knowing spiritual "honey," says: "finding honey, eat what is enough." But with what understanding did the Holy Spirit enjoin upon us that, "if we have found honey" — since "honey" is indeed findable — "we should eat what is enough"? "Go," he says, "to the bee and learn how she is a worker." And the prophets are found to be "bees," for they fashion wax and make "honey," and, if it is fitting for me to venture to say it, their "honeycombs" are the scriptures which they have left behind. And if you are willing, come to the scriptures and you will find "honey." But also: "eat honey," and again in Proverbs it is said: "for a honeycomb is good, that your throat may be sweetened." Do you suppose the Holy Spirit says this — "eat honey" — of that which is in common use, "for it is good"? I do not dare to say that the Holy Spirit enjoins upon me concerning bodily "honey": "eat honey." Behold, I do not have it, or else I am of such a nature that I cannot "eat honey"; by what reasoning does he say to me: "eat honey," and do not "eat" flesh, but "eat, my son, honey, for it is good"? If you see that the prophets are "bees" and their work "honey" or "honeycombs," then you will see how, in a manner worthy of the Holy Spirit, you may understand "eat, my son, honey, for it is good." If anyone meditates on the divine oracles and is nourished by the words of the scriptures, he fulfills the command that bids: "eat, my son, honey," and, doing what is commanded, he takes possession of the word that follows: "for it is good," because "good" is this "honey" which is found in the scriptures. And what is said, "go to the bee," is of this kind. There is, so to speak, a certain "bee" above the bees; and just as among bees there is a certain king who is named to be king, so the prince of the bees is my Lord Jesus Christ, to whom the Holy Spirit sends me, that "I may eat honey, for it is good, and his honeycombs, that my throat may be sweetened." And perhaps the finer letters will be "honeycombs"; but the "honey" is the understanding that is in them. This one, moreover, who is born of the "virgin, Emmanuel, eats butter and honey" and seeks from each one of us "to eat butter." How he seeks "butter" and "honey" from each of us, the word will teach. Our sweet works, our words most pleasant and useful, are "honey" which "Emmanuel eats," which this one "eats" who was born of the "virgin." But if our words are full of bitterness — anger, animosity, sadness, filthy speech, vices, contention — they have put gall in my mouth, and the Savior does not "eat" of these words. But the Savior "will eat" of the words that are among men, if their words are "honey." Let us confirm this from the scriptures. "Behold, I have stood before the door and I knock; if anyone opens the door to me, I will come in to him and sup with him, and he with me." Therefore he himself promises that he "will sup with us" from our own things. And it is certain that we too "sup with" him, if we "sup upon him." For "eating" of our good words, works, and understanding, he feeds us again with his own spiritual and divine and better foods. Therefore, since it is a blessed thing to receive the Savior, let us, with the doors of the ruling part of our heart opened, prepare for him "honey" and all his supper, that he himself may lead us to the great supper of the Father in the kingdom of heaven, which is in Christ Jesus, "to whom is glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen!"
Commentary on Isaiah

He shall eat butter and honey, that he may know to refuse evil and to choose good. For which the Seventy translated before he knows; and what follows, to take up evil, is not found in the Hebrew. And the sense is: O House of David, who are commanded by the word of God to call, that is, to call upon, when set in danger, the name of Emmanuel, that is, of God with us: do not marvel at the novelty of the thing, if a Virgin bears God, who has such power that, though he is to be born a long time after, being called upon he frees you now; for he it is who was seen by Abraham and spoke with Moses. I will tell you something else more marvelous, lest you think he will be born in a phantasm: he will use the foods of infancy, he will eat butter and milk. And although many ages later the Evangelist testifies of him: And the child advanced in wisdom and age and grace with God and men (Luke 2:52), and this is said so that the reality of his human body may be proved; yet while still wrapped in swaddling clothes, and fed on butter and honey, he will have judgment of good and evil, so that refusing evil things he chooses good things. Not that he did this, or refused, or chose; but that he knew how to refuse and to choose, so that by these words we may know that the infancy of the human body did not prejudice the divine wisdom. Indeed, the Angels announce him to the shepherds as he lies in the manger; the Magi, coming from the East, worship him, who surely, we must believe, were chosen. And on the contrary, Herod, the Scribes and the Pharisees are refused (Matt 2), because for the sake of one infant they slaughtered many thousands of little ones.
Commentary on Isaiah

For before the child knows to refuse evil and to choose good, the land which you abhor shall be forsaken before the face of its two kings. In the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule Samaria was taken by the Assyrians (2 Kgs 18), that is, in the thirty-first year of his age. If, then, this one who is to be born, whether of a Virgin, as we prove, or of a young woman, as the Jews would have it, will eat butter and honey, and will be so small that he cannot distinguish evil from good, and before he passes beyond the time of infancy the land of Syria and of Samaria is to be laid waste by the Assyrians: let the Hebrews answer how Hezekiah at thirty-one years is proclaimed a little infant, and of such untrained age that, eating honey and butter, like the children of Nineveh, he knows neither left nor right, that is, neither evil nor good. But referred to Emmanuel, which is interpreted God with us, it will have an easy understanding: that at the mystery and the invocation of his name the land of Syria and of Samaria is laid waste by the conquering Assyrian, and the house of David is freed from the two kings whom it fears, namely Rezin and Pekah.
Commentary on Isaiah

The Lord will bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days that have not come since the days of the separation of Ephraim from Judah, with the king of the Assyrians. This place is to be read by hyperbaton. Indeed we too, following the Hebrew truth, have interpreted it thus: O house of David, listen to what I say: so that the land of Syria and Samaria may be forsaken before the face of the two kings whom you most vehemently dread, the Lord will bring days upon you, and upon the house of your father David, such as you have never had from the time when the ten tribes were separated from the two tribes and began to have a kingdom in Samaria. And he will bring those days, that is, times, with the king of the Assyrians, so that when those kings have been conquered and overthrown, you may be freed by the presence of Emmanuel. The Seventy rendered this place thus: The Lord will bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days which have not yet come, from the day on which Ephraim took away the king of the Assyrians from Judah. What sense this has we cannot know, unless perhaps this must be said: that Ephraim, that is, Samaria, by the greatness of its sins first made the onslaught of the Assyrians turn aside to itself. Otherwise: For the meantime now the two kings Rezin and Pekah, who besiege you and hasten to lay you waste, will be overthrown in a short time; but the time of your own laying waste will come when the Assyrian comes, which you had never expected, indeed never feared. By which he teaches that the house of David must fear not Syria and Samaria but the Assyrians. So he frees it from the present dread, and threatens concerning the time to come.
Commentary on Isaiah

And it shall be in that day, the Lord will whistle for the fly that is at the farthest part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria: and they shall come and shall all rest in the torrents of the valleys, and in the caves of the rocks, and in all the thickets, and in all the holes. When the land of the two kings, Damascus and Samaria, which you now abhor and fear, has been deserted, then, O house of Judah, the Lord will bring upon you and your people days such as you have never seen before, and the king of the Assyrians. In vain, therefore, do you fear things present, half-burnt brands that have no fire at all: for you ought to know that with his whistle the Lord is going to call the flies of Egypt and of its rivers, by which without doubt he means the seven διωρυχὰς of the Nile, and the bee that is in the land of Assyria. And he calls the Egyptians flies on account of the filth of idolatry and because they were an unwarlike people; and the Assyrians a bee, whose kingdom at that time was the most powerful and the readiest for wars; or for this reason, that almost the whole region of the Assyrians and of Persia made use of arrows. These, then, will all come and occupy your land, in the torrents of the valleys, and the caves of the rocks, and in all the thickets and holes, and in the leafy woods. These things are said by metaphor, so that, since he had once named flies and bees, he might keep the figure in the rest. Let us read the books of Kings and Chronicles, and we shall find that the holy king Josiah was slain by the Egyptians, and the people of Israel subjugated to the Egyptian power (2 Kgs 23; 2 Chr 35), so that it appointed a king for them. And not long after, Nebuchadnezzar came with a countless multitude of warriors, and having taken Jerusalem and torn down the other cities of Judea, he burned the Temple and settled Assyrian inhabitants in Judea (2 Kgs 24).
Commentary on Isaiah

In that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor, by those who are beyond the river, by the king of the Assyrians, the head, and the hair of the feet, and the whole beard. Some think that this is prophesied of the Assyrians, who for thirteen hundred years before they overthrew Jerusalem possessed the kingdom of Asia, of Egypt and of Libya: that they were to be conquered by the Medes and Persians and their empire destroyed. Others, however, judge that the Egyptians were slain beyond the river Euphrates. But we judge that the razor hired for a wage is the Assyrian himself, whom in Jeremiah, for the punishment of the sinful people, he even calls his dove (Jer 25). Indeed in the vision of Tyre too (Ezek 29:18-20), because Nebuchadnezzar had toiled very greatly in building siege-works and in heaping up a mound, and, when they fled by fleet, had been deprived of his wage, Egypt was given to him as the wage for his labor. So with this most sharp razor, and by those who dwell beyond the river Euphrates, namely by the Assyrian king, the Lord will shave from Judea all the hair and the hairs of the whole body from head to feet, and the comeliness of the beard, which is the mark of manhood, so that nothing strong, nothing beautiful may remain in it, but they may be compared to effeminate men, or rather to disgraced women.
Commentary on Isaiah

And it shall be in that day, a man shall rear a cow of the herd and two sheep, and for the abundance of milk he shall eat butter: for everyone who is left in the midst of the land shall eat butter and honey. And it shall be in that day, every place where there were a thousand vines at a thousand pieces of silver shall become thorns and briers. With arrows and bow they shall go in there: for briers and thorns shall be in all the land. And all the mountains that shall be hoed with the hoe, the terror of thorns and briers shall not come there: and it shall be for the pasture of the ox and for the treading of the flock. After the overthrow of Jerusalem, and the captivity of the people, and the burning of the Temple, Nebuzaradan the chief of the soldiery, whom the Seventy call ἀρχιμάγειρον, left in the land a few of the people, and those poor, to till the vineyards and fields. Then Gedaliah, who, left from the royal line, had been set over them, exhorts them and says: Do not fear the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you (2 Kgs 25:24). In that day, then, that is, at that time, when all the wealth of the Jews has been carried off into Chaldea, so great will be the desolation in the land of Judea, and so incredible the devastation, that they will by no means have herds of oxen, nor flocks of sheep, as they had been accustomed to have before; but a rare inhabitant will scarcely be able to rear one cow and two sheep; not for ploughing, but for the food of their milk and the clothing of their fleece. For through the want of grain and of everything that the earth brings forth for eating, they will feed on milk and butter and wild honey. And what he says, For the abundance of milk he shall eat butter, signifies this: that the land, through the scarcity of tillers, is more fertile and better suited for pastures.
Commentary on Isaiah

Would that we did not know that these things are wont to happen after a captivity! But now a great part of the Roman world is like Judea of old: which we do not think has come about without the wrath of God, who avenges contempt of himself not through Assyrians and Chaldeans, but through savage nations, once unknown to us, whose countenance and speech alike are terrible, and who, displaying womanish and shaven faces [he means the Goths, who shaved their beards], stab the fleeing backs of men, and well-bearded men at that. I know that I have read in these places a very broad and inextricable tropology: that all the things we have set out according to the history happened spiritually to the Jews, who scarcely have one cow and two sheep, that is, clean animals: so that they are nourished not on solid food but on the milk of infancy, and eat the honey of words that drips from the lips of the harlot woman; and they do not have wine, which gladdens the heart of man, but all their works are reduced to thorns, so that they are wounded by adversaries who shoot in the dark at the upright of heart (Ps 10 [11]). And if at any time they wish to be wise in something higher, and, sweating with excessive labor, to find something mystical in the holy Scriptures, nonetheless they bring forth no fruits of doctrine, but are filled with briers and thorns, which spring up in the hands of a drunkard. And their land and doctrine is trodden down not by men, rational living beings, but by oxen, for whom God has no care, and by brute animals.
Commentary on Isaiah

At that time, through the fewness of men, so great will be the want of wine, the vineyards being deserted and by no means pruned for fear of the enemy, that single vines will scarcely be bought for single silver shekels.
Commentary on Isaiah

For the whole land will be reduced to briers and thorns; and so great will be the dread, with swords raging everywhere, that no one will dare to visit his own field without bow and arrows, and, abandoning the places in the plains, they will flee to the mountains, and there, protected by the difficulty of the places, they will scarcely dig the rough mountains by hand: because they will not have oxen, ploughs and ploughshares. Wherever, then, a rare tiller is found in the mountains, they will sustain a miserable life from there. But the rest will lie open to pastures, and will be trodden down by brute animals without any keeper.

h.p: < Previous Chapter ----- Next Chapter > Isaias viii. Notes & Commentary:
n: Book. This mystery would require a large explanation. (Worthington) --- Pen. Literally, "style." (Haydock) --- Write intelligibly. Here all is plain. (Calmet) --- Take. Protestants, "concerning Mahershalalchashbaz." Marginal note, "in making speed to the spoil, he hasteneth the prey." (Haydock) --- Chashbaz, the son of Isaias, was a sign that Syria and Israel should soon be rendered desolate; and in a more elevated sense, he shewed that Christ should overturn the powers of hell. (Calmet) --- The virgin's son [Jesus Christ] took the prey from the devil, who before possessed almost all the world. (Worthington) --- Urias. Probably the high priest, who afterwards weakly complied with the king's idolatrous order, 4 Kings xvi. 10. (Calmet) --- Yet at this time, he was a credible witness. (Haydock) --- Zacharias. A person to us unknown. (Calmet)

Prophetess. The blessed Virgin [Mary], (St. Chrysostom, &c.) or to his wife. He gives his son a different name from Emmanuel, (chap. vii. 14.) that they might not be confounded. --- Hasten. Hebrew Mahershalalchashbaz, ver. 1. (Haydock)

Assyrians. Theglathphalassar, the next year, took the Damascenes to Kir, and Nephthali, Reuben, Gad, and Manasses into captivity. Yet the kingdom continued some time longer. Never was prediction more explicit. Can the pagans produce any thing similar?

Silence. Being willing to receive Tabeel, instead of their lawful prince. Achaz was then terrified, and chose to become tributary, rather than to lose his crown. Herein both offended God, in whom they ought to have trusted; and the auxiliary king looked upon himself as master of the country, 2 Paralipomenon xxviii. 20. (Calmet) --- Israel had joined with the Syrian; but was reduced to the state of captivity, while Jerusalem was preserved. (Worthington)
River. Euphrates, (Calmet) with the overflowing of which the Assyrian is compared. (Haydock)
Wings. Or troops. --- Emmanuel. Christ was born in the country, and Lord of it: though it might be said to belong to the son of Isaias, as being his figure. (Calmet)
Overcome. The defeat of Sennacherib, of the Idumeans, &c., under Ezechias, is intimated, 4 Kings xviii. 8., and xix. 35.
God. Hebrew, "Emmanuel." We have a pledge of God's protection.
Conspiracy. In despair, they wish to submit to the enemy, ver. 6. Isaias exhorts them to have recourse rather to the Lord. (Calmet)
Two. The wicked of both kingdoms, (Haydock) who choose to revolt from God. Many of Israel were led into captivity, and the territory of Juda was laid waste. (Calmet)
Disciples. Let some faithful witnesses keep this prophecy, (Haydock) that when it is verified, all may be convinced.
Jacob. Having resolved on their ruin. (Calmet)

I and my two children. Chap. vii. 3., and viii. 4. (Haydock) --- The actions of some were prophetical, chap. xx. 2., and Osee xii. 10. (Calmet) --- God announces what will happen, by the names of my children, (Haydock) and by their age, as well as by my mouth. (Calmet)

Seek of pythons. That is, people pretending to tell future things by a prophesying spirit. --- Should not the people seek of their God, for the living of the dead? Here is signified, that it is to God we should pray to be directed, and not to seek of the dead, (that is, of fortune-tellers dead in sin) for the health of the living. (Challoner) --- Mutter. Literally, "use a shrill note," strident. (Haydock) --- So Horace, (1 Sat. viii.) says: Umbræ cum sagana resonarent triste et acutum. --- Should. Make this reply: Should, &c.

Law. Sealed, (ver. 16.) or to the law of Moses, Ecclesiasticus xxxiv. 28. (Calmet) --- Septuagint, "why do they consult the dead concerning the living? For he gave the law to assist us." (Haydock) --- Light. They shall die or be miserable. (Calmet)
By it. The word of God. (Haydock) --- God. Elohim means also princes or idols. (Calmet) --- Whether they seek God unwillingly, or the aid of men, (ver. 22.) they shall perish. (Worthington)

f: Commentary on Isaiah

And the Lord said to me: Take for yourself a great book, and write in it with the pen of a man: Swiftly strip the spoils, quickly take the prey. And I took to me faithful witnesses, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Barachiah, and I went in to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me: Call his name, Make haste, strip the spoils, hasten to take the prey: for before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of the Assyrians. The Seventy, for a great book, translated a new and great book. And in place of what is found in the Hebrew, I took to me faithful witnesses, they said: for it is at hand, and make faithful men witnesses for me. And for Uriah the Priest, only Uriah; the rest likewise. First the Prophet was sent to Ahaz (Isa 7), to foretell to him what the Scripture records: when he would not listen, the Lord himself speaks to Ahaz, and commanded him to ask for himself a sign in the depth or in the height. When he answered, I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord, the impious king is dismissed and the words of God are turned to the house of David, and there is promised to it a Virgin who will bear a son, whose name is to be Emmanuel, that is, God with us. If he is called upon often, Samaria and Syria will be overthrown: overthrown, however, by the king of the Assyrians, who is afterward to capture Judah itself too; so that the whole land of Judea is turned into a wilderness. So again, under another figure, the virginal birth is described. And the Lord told the Prophet not at all to bring out the secret of the new birth among the peoples, but to write it in this great volume which we now read. And, that it may be the more marvelous, to comprise the mysteries of God in human words, and with the pen with which men are accustomed to write. And what is it that is written with a human pen? That the child who is born should swiftly strip the spoils and quickly take the prey, that is, that he should no longer suffer the devil to reign; nor send Angels nor Prophets, but himself come down to save his creatures. So the Prophet does what was commanded, and takes to himself two faithful witnesses: Uriah the priest, who is a teacher of the law, as Malachi says: The lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law from his mouth, for he is the Angel of the Lord of hosts (Mal 2:7); and Zechariah the son of Barachiah, who, there is no doubt, was a Prophet. We read that in the reign of Ahaz, Uriah was priest of the Temple of the Lord (2 Kgs 16), whom Ahaz commanded to make an altar like the altar of Damascus. And the book of Days relates (2 Chr 29) that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz sought the Lord in the days of Zechariah, who was instructed in the fear of God.
Commentary on Isaiah

Uriah is interpreted light of the Lord; Zechariah, memory of the Lord; and Barachiah, blessing of the Lord: by these witnesses the birth of Christ is proved. For he himself in the Gospel, to the two who were going to Emmaus (Luke 24), beginning from Moses and the Prophets, set out that all things had prophesied of him. According to tropology, in a virginal soul, stained by no filth, the word of God, conceived of the Holy Spirit, swiftly strips the spoils from the adverse powers and makes all things serve him. And since it now sees in part and prophesies in part (1 Cor 13), before it can be perfect and rightly call God its Father and the heavenly Jerusalem its mother, while still set in infancy and in progress, it will overcome the strength of Damascus, namely the doctrine of secular wisdom; and will take away the spoils of Samaria, with which the heretics have despoiled the Church, saying: We have no portion in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse (1 Kgs 12:16), in the presence of the king of the Assyrians himself, the devil, who will not be able to help them. And such sons are borne not only by Mary, the perpetual Virgin, to the Prophets, but also by holy women to the patriarchs: Sarah, which is interpreted ἄρχουσα, that is, princess; and Rebecca, which in our language sounds patience.
HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 5:2

How was it then, one may say, that His name was not called Emmanuel, but Jesus Christ? Because he said not, "thou shalt call," but "they shall call," that is, the multitude, and the issue of events. For here he puts the event as a name: and this is customary in Scripture, to substitute the events that take place for names. Therefore, to say, "they shall call" Him "Emmanuel," means nothing else than that they shall see God amongst men. For He hath indeed always been amongst men, but never so manifestly.
Commentary on Isaiah

And Isaiah showed himself worthy of the prophetic spirit, and offered himself to the prophetess, that is, to the Holy Spirit, which in the Hebrew speech is called in the feminine gender RUA (רוה), according to what is written: Draw near to the Lord, and be enlightened (Ps 33 [34]:6). So the Lord was conceived of the Holy Spirit. And although human speech cannot unfold the mysteries of his birth, yet Gabriel speaks to the Virgin herself who conceived: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you: therefore the holy thing that will be born of you will be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). Some interpret the prophetess as holy Mary, who, there is no doubt, was a prophetess: for she herself says in the Gospel: For behold, from henceforth all generations will call me blessed: for he who is mighty has done great things for me (Luke 1:48-49), and the rest. And Isaiah is commanded to call that very child, who before was called Emmanuel, now Make haste, strip the spoils, hasten to take the prey. For ascending on high he led captivity captive; he received gifts for men (Ps 67 [68]; Eph 4:8). And before he took a human body and, in the manner of infancy, called God his father and Mary his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be taken away by the king of the Assyrians: so that, not yet born, he might save his people, the house of David, by invocation alone.
Dialogue with Trypho, Chapter LXXVIII

For that expression of Isaiah 'He shall take the power of Damascus and spoils of Samaria,' foretold that the power of the evil demon that dwelt in Damascus should be overcome by Christ as soon as He was born; and this is proved to have happened. For the Magi, who were held in bondage for the commission of all evil deeds through the power of that demon, by coming to worship Christ, shows that they have revolted from that dominion which held them captive; and this [dominion] the Scripture has showed us to reside in Damascus. Moreover, that sinful and unjust power is termed well in parable, Samaria. And none of you can deny that Damascus was, and is, in the region of Arabia, although now it belongs to what is called Syrophoenicia. Hence it would be becoming for you, sirs, to learn what you have not perceived, from those who have received grace from God, namely, from us Christians; and not to strive in every way to maintain your own doctrines, dishonouring those of God.
The Five Books Against Marcion, Book 5

I, on my part, now wish to engage with you in a discussion on the allegorical expressions of the apostle. What figures of speech could the novel god have found in the prophets (fit for himself)? "He led captivity captive," [Ephesians 4:8] says the apostle. With what arms? In what conflicts? From the devastation of what country? From the overthrow of what city? What women, what children, what princes did the Conqueror throw into chains? For when by David Christ is sung as "girded with His sword upon His thigh," [Psalm 45:3] or by Isaiah as "taking away the spoils of Samaria and the power of Damascus," [Isaiah 8:4] you make Him out to be really and truly a warrior confest to the eye. Learn then now, that His is a spiritual armour and warfare, since you have already discovered that the captivity is spiritual, in order that you may further learn that this also belongs to Him, even because the apostle derived the mention of the captivity from the same prophets as suggested to him his precepts likewise: ...
SERMON 202:2

For, before the child knew how to call his father and mother, as Isaiah had prophesied of him, he took the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria. That is, before he uttered human speech through his humanity, he took the strength of Damascus or that which gave confidence to Damascus. For, in the estimation of the world, that city had flourished for some time on account of her riches. But preeminence in riches is gained by gold, and the magi as suppliants offered gold to Christ.
Commentary on Isaiah

And the Lord spoke to me yet again, saying: Because this people has cast away the waters of Siloam that go in silence, and has rather taken up Rezin and the son of Remaliah: therefore behold, the Lord will bring upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, the king of the Assyrians and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and shall flow over all his banks. And he shall go through Judah overflowing, and passing through he shall come up to the neck, and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of your land, O Emmanuel. He had said above that the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria were to be taken away in the sight of the king of the Assyrians, and that the two kings would be captured when the Assyrian made war: now God speaks to the Prophet in the customary character of the Scriptures, by a figure of Siloam, the spring of Jerusalem, and of the most violent Assyrian river, that it would flood the whole land of Israel with its waters, and go out over the banks of its bed, and be borne with such force that, after it had occupied the land of the ten tribes, it would reach Judah and, passing through, would extend up to the neck: by which he signifies the captivity close at hand. For Judah was not captured at that time, but when all the cities of the two tribes had been subjugated, Jerusalem alone remained, which was freed by the incredible mercy of God. So the might of the Assyrian and of his countless army, which he had described under the flooding of a river, he now shows by another figure: that with his wings, that is, his generals and boundless multitude, he covered the land of Emmanuel, that is, of God who defends it, but yet did not possess it; although Emmanuel is fitted by the Seventy to the following section, not with its proper name, as it is called among the Hebrews, but translated, that is, God with us. And that Siloam is a spring at the roots of Mount Zion, which bubbles up not with continuous waters but at certain hours and days, and comes through hollows of the earth and caves of the hardest rock with a great sound, we cannot doubt, we especially who dwell in this province. And the sense is: because the people of the ten tribes preferred to be subject to Rezin and the son of Remaliah, that is, to the kings of Damascus and Samaria, rather than to the stock of David, which began to reign by my judgment, I will make it serve not at all these kings whom it has taken up, but the Assyrian king, whose might as it occupies the land of Samaria is compared to the flooding of a river. And an apostrophe is made to Emmanuel, that is, to God present, because the Assyrian raised himself up so far as to try to possess even his land, Judah. According to the anagogy, every heretic who joins secular wisdom to his help and seeks to attack Jerusalem, that is, the Church, forsaking the waters of the spring Siloam (John 9), which is interpreted sent, and which leaps up to eternal life, will be handed over to the prince of the Assyrians (whom we shall read of later as the great mind), and, handed over to his power, he will come into the depth of sins. For he is of such arrogance that he dared to show the Savior all the kingdoms of the earth and to say: All these have been handed over to me (Matt and Luke 4). He will try also to enter Judah, that is, the house of confession, and often, through those in the Church who are negligent, he will come up to the neck, desiring to choke those who believe in Christ, and he will stretch out his wings, filling the whole region of Emmanuel; but he will not be able to prevail, because Judah has God present. We read in the Gospel according to John (John 9) that the Lord sent the man blind from birth, whose eyes he had anointed with clay made from his spittle, to the waters of Siloam, and when the blind man had washed off the clay in them, his blindness was wiped away and he received the clear light of his eyes: which, beyond the greatness of the sign, indicates that the blindness of the Jews and of every unbeliever cannot be healed otherwise than if the darkness of former error is put to flight by the doctrine of the waters of Christ, which flows gently without the din and clamor of words. This which is read in the Seventy: And he will walk over all your wall, and will take away from Judea the man who can lift up his head or perhaps do anything, is not found in the Hebrew, and in the Greek codices it has been pierced through with ÷ the slaying spit.
ON FIRST PRINCIPLES 4:1.5

And what the same prophet said has been fulfilled. "God is with us. Know this, O nations, and be conquered." For we who are from the nations have been conquered and overcome. And we who bend our necks beneath his grace stand forth as a kind of spoils of his victory.
Commentary on Isaiah

Gather together, O peoples, and be conquered, and hear, all you lands far off: take strength, and be conquered. Gird yourselves, and be conquered: take counsel, and it shall be scattered: speak a word, and it shall not be done, for God is with us. For gather together, or be weak and be broken, as others interpreted, the Seventy set know. For the Hebrew word ROU (רעו), because of the likeness of the letter RES (ר) and DALETH (ד), they understood as DOU (דעו). So, O peoples of Samaria and Syria, know that you are weak and feeble, and that with Emmanuel present you can do nothing against Jerusalem, the city of God: and let not only you, who are neighbors, know this, but the whole land far off. For although you gather an army and gird yourselves for battle, and the number of the besiegers is greater than that of the besieged, yet not once but a second time I will say: you are conquered. And whatever counsel you take against Jerusalem will be scattered. And although you said above (Isa 7:6): Let us go up to Judah, and rouse it up while it is at rest, and set over it as king the son of Tabeel, you speak a word indeed, but it will not be done, because God is with us, that is, Emmanuel. We can use this testimony against the gentiles too in time of persecution: that although they seem strong and to overcome us in those who have lapsed, yet they are conquered in those who have shed their blood for Christ, and that after wars peace is restored to the Churches, and all their counsels against Emmanuel are scattered, because God is with us. Those who contradict the truth will also profitably hear it, so that at last they may be overcome by reason, and may not wish to win in falsehood, because whatever they say, perversity can never overcome what is right.
Commentary on Isaiah

For thus the Lord says to me: As with a strong hand he instructed me, that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying: Do not say, A conspiracy; for all that this people speaks is a conspiracy: and do not fear its fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself: let him be your dread, and let him be your terror. And he shall be for a sanctification to you, but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel: for a snare and for a ruin to those who dwell in Jerusalem; and very many of them shall stumble, and shall fall, and shall be broken, and shall be ensnared, and shall be taken. The Seventy translated this place thus: Thus says the Lord: With a strong hand they have withdrawn from the journey of the way of this people, saying: Lest perhaps they say, It is hard. For all that this people speaks is hard; but do not fear its fear, nor be troubled. Sanctify the Lord of powers himself, and he shall be your fear, and if you have trusted in him, he shall be for a sanctification to you, and you shall not run against him as against a stone of stumbling, nor as against a rock of ruin. But the house of Jacob shall be in a snare and in a valley for those who sit in Jerusalem: therefore very many among them shall be weak, and shall fall and be broken, and shall draw near, and shall be taken. And what follows, men in safekeeping, is to be marked in front with an obelus. Because the Hebrew and the common edition differ much from each other, we have therefore set down both. And first we must discuss the Hebrew. Thus the Lord spoke to me. Who, on account of good works, and the grace which on account of good works I have obtained; or with his strong hand instructed and trained me, that I should not walk in the way of this people and be held in the same error; or certainly he made me withdraw from the most evil way of this people, and said to me: do not fear the conspiracy of the two kings; but consider this rather, that all that this people speaks against me is a conspiracy; and, according to Symmachus, who interpreted ἄνταρσιν, has risen up against me in rebellion. But you, Prophet, and those who are with you, do not fear the plots of the people, but fear the Lord, and let him be your fear. For the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom (Prov 1:7; Ps 110 [111]:9).
Commentary on Isaiah

According to the Seventy, the people resisted the will of God with a strong hand, and says that all that the Lord has commanded is hard, according to what we read in the Gospel: This saying is hard; who can hear it (John 6:61)? Hence they are commanded to hear the Lord and to fear him alone.
Commentary on Isaiah

He will be for a sanctification to believers, but to unbelievers for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, that is, to the two houses of Judah and Israel; and especially for a snare and a ruin to those who dwell in Jerusalem, on whom very many will strike, and will fall, and will be broken, and, ensnared in the chains of their sins, will be led into captivity. The two houses the Nazaraeans (who receive Christ in such a way that they do not give up the observances of the old Law) interpret as two families, Shammai and Hillel, from whom arose the Scribes and Pharisees, whose school Akiba took over, whom they assert to have been the teacher of Aquila the proselyte, and after him Meir, whom Johanan the son of Zakkai succeeded, and after him Eliezer, and in order Telphon, and again Joseph the Galilean, and up to the capture of Jerusalem Joshua. So Shammai and Hillel arose in Judea not long before the Lord was born, of whom the former is interpreted scatterer, the latter profane: because by their traditions and δευτερώσεις they scattered and defiled the precepts of the Law. And that these are the two houses which did not receive the Savior, who became for them a ruin and an offense.
Commentary on Isaiah

For if they have trusted in him, they will have him for a sanctification, and will not strike against him as against a stone of offense and as against a rock of ruin. From this place the Apostle too takes a testimony, that Christ became an offense to the Jews, but to the Gentiles foolishness (1 Cor 1:23). And again: Israel, by pursuing the law of righteousness, has not attained to the law of righteousness (Rom 9:31). Why? Because not from faith, but as if from the works of the law, they stumbled against the stone of stumbling, as it is written: Behold, I will lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense: everyone who believes in him shall not be put to shame (ibid., 33). So those who did not receive Emmanuel, but for whom he became a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, will be broken and led captive. And what he says, But the house of Jacob shall be in a snare and in a valley for those who sit in Jerusalem, signifies this: that they do not dwell on the mountains, nor move in the lofty places of the Scriptures, but always understand lowly things, joining sins to sins, and bound by the snares of their offenses.
Commentary on Matthew

On that day the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. There were two heresies among the Jews, one of the Pharisees and the other of the Sadducees. The Pharisees held up a righteousness of traditions and observances, which they call deuteroses, and hence they were also called 'divided' by the people; while the Sadducees, which is interpreted 'just', themselves also claimed for themselves what they were not. And whereas the former believed and confessed the resurrection of both body and soul, and angels and spirit, the latter, according to the Acts of the Apostles, denied it all. These are the two houses of which Isaiah teaches quite plainly that they would stumble on the stone of stumbling.
SERMON 92:2

Christ rose again from the seed of David, as the son of David, because he had emptied himself. How did he empty himself? By taking what he was not, not by losing what he was. He emptied himself; he humbled himself. Though he was God, he made himself known as a man. He was despised as he walked the earth, though he made the sky. He was despised as a mere man, as though he had no power. Not only despised, but on top of that also killed. He was a stone lying flat; the Jews stumbled over him and were shaken. But what does he say about that himself? "Whoever stumbles over this stone will be shaken; but as for anyone upon whom this stone comes, it will crush him." First he lay flat, and they stumbled; he will come from above and crush them, after they have been shaken.
Commentary on Isaiah

Hence the Prophet answered: Because, the Gospel taking its place, the Law has been shut and sealed among the Jews, and you command that it be assigned not at all to the Jews but to the nations: therefore I will wait for Emmanuel, whom you promise is to come, of whom you said above that he himself is our dread and he himself our terror, and that he is for a sanctification to us; and I will look for the Lord who hides his face from the house of Jacob, that is, from the Jews, because they would not receive him. The Seventy translated this place thus: Then they who are sealed shall be manifest, that they may not learn the law. Which has this sense: when very many have fallen and been broken, and have struck against the stone of stumbling and the rock of offense, then those who are sealed among the people will be manifest, so that they may by no means learn the law of Moses, but obey the precepts of the Gospel.
Commentary on Isaiah

Bind up the testimonies, seal the law among my disciples, and I will wait for the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. The voice of the Lord speaking to the Prophet: Because, he says, the Lord has become a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel, and they would not receive Emmanuel sent to them: Bind up the testimonies of the old Instrument, and hand them over to my disciples, who have received the Gospel, namely the Apostles, or apostolic men. Or certainly, let the law and the prophecy until John be bound up among them (Matt 11), and be shut and sealed, so that what they read they may not understand. For in place of disciples, according to the ambiguity of the Hebrew speech, we can also interpret doctrines.
HOMILIES ON ISAIAH 7

"Give a wise man an occasion, and he will be the wiser," said the divine saying. Taking, then, our "occasion" from the most sacred Apostles for the understanding of the prophetic words, let us pray to God that we may receive wisdom and be able to become "the wiser" through the "occasion" of the Apostles for expounding the prophets. The Apostle, recalling this saying, "Behold, I and the children whom God has given me," then goes on and expounds: "Since therefore the children shared in blood and flesh, he too became near to them, being made a partaker of theirs, that through death he might destroy him who had the dominion of death, that is, the devil, and deliver those who through fear of death were, throughout their whole life, subject to the guilt of bondage." Therefore, "since the children were made partakers of blood and flesh," our Savior too "shared in blood and flesh." For it was foreign to his nature and his divinity to take up "blood and flesh"; but for our sake he took up those things which were foreign to him, that he might make us his own household, who had been made foreign through sin. And the Apostle indeed expounded it thus, saying: "Since therefore the children shared in blood and flesh, he too became near to them, being made a partaker of theirs"; but I would say that, just as "since the children shared in blood and flesh, he too became near to them, being made a partaker of theirs," so, since the "children" cannot hear the stronger discourses — for they must, as "children," hear the words of God — for this reason, having been "made present" in the "blood of the children" for the sake of those who "shared in flesh and blood," speaking "as to little ones," he speaks not divine and unutterable things, but only such things as "little ones" can grasp. And "little ones" are all men, if you compare them to the perfection of the Word; you may name Moses, you may name one of the prophets, you may name John, than whom "there was none greater among those born of women," you may come to the Apostles, to Peter, against whom "the gates of hell shall not prevail," or to Paul, who "was caught up to the third heaven and heard unspeakable words" — you do not lower their glory by saying that they too, in the things they understood, in comparison with the things they did not understand, were trained in the disciplines of "little ones," which are handed down to men. The Savior therefore speaks not of those whom Paul calls "little ones" in Christ and declares must be "given milk to drink" and not "solid food," but of all men together: "Behold, I and my little ones, whom God has given me." But just as among "children" some are more eager than others and more quickly attain the things handed down to them, so, I say, Moses and the prophets, and also the Apostles of the Lord Jesus Christ, were made like gifted "children." Therefore, being aware of themselves — that, even if they made progress, they made the progress of "children" — they said: "We know in part and we prophesy in part." For they did not yet behold the realities of truth, but the shadows of the realities, nor the full light, but a dim image; and so they repeated, saying: "For now we see through a glass and in a riddle, but then face to face." Who then, reading and understanding these things, will be puffed up and exalt himself over his knowledge, or over any of the gifts? For since the things which have come to "children" are far inferior to those which are reserved for grown men, those who seem among the "children" to be of keener and quicker wit ought not to be lifted up and grow proud. And these "children" he calls all men, whom the Savior also pointed out, saying: "Behold, I and the children whom God has given me." The Savior too received a gift from God; for "no one comes to" him, "unless he who sent" him "has drawn" the one coming to the Savior, as we have learned in the Gospel which is according to John. And because he received from the Father, as a gift, those who believe, therefore, prophesying about them, he says: "Behold, I and the children whom God has given me." Nor is he who received to be thought to be without them, since he who "gave" still has them himself.
HOMILIES ON ISAIAH 7

Then in what follows the Savior prophesies in the prophet, saying that it will come to pass that, when he has received the "children," "signs and wonders shall come to pass in Israel." For it stands thus: "And there shall be signs and wonders in Israel from the Lord of Sabaoth, who dwells on Mount Zion." For he who "dwells in" the watchtower and can behold the truth in every soul, he it is who works "signs and wonders" through the Savior, and after the Savior through the Apostles; and wherever a soul is found fit for the ministry of the "signs and portents" of God — whether according to spiritual healing or perceptibly, for exhorting to faith those who see — God, who then wrought "signs and wonders," is not idle to work them even now.
Commentary on Isaiah

Behold, I and my children, whom the Lord has given me for signs and portents of Israel, from the Lord of hosts who dwells on Mount Zion. The Lord, he says, commanded me to bind up the testimony among the Jews and to hand over and seal the law for his disciples, because he had hidden his face from the house of Jacob: therefore I will look for him and wait for my Lord, and not only I, but also the children whom the Lord has given me, namely the other prophets and the sons of the prophets, who were born not of the will of the flesh and of blood, but of God (John 1:13). Of whom the Apostle too spoke: My little children, with whom I am again in travail until Christ be formed in you (Gal 4:19). And these children, that is, the prophets, were given for signs and for portents to Israel, according to what we read in Ezekiel: And Ezekiel shall be for a sign to you (Ezek 24:24). In Zechariah too, holy men and disciples of the prophets are called τερατοσκόποι, that is, watchers of portents and signs, because the Prophets always went before as a sign of things to come (Zech 3:8). This much meanwhile according to the letter. But the blessed Apostle, in the Epistle which is written to the Hebrews (though Latin custom does not receive it among the canonical Scriptures), teaches that this testimony ought to be understood in the person of the Lord and Savior: For which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying: I will announce your name to my brothers, in the midst of the Church I will praise you (Heb 2:12); and again: I will put my trust in him (ibid., 13); and once more: Behold, I and my children, whom God has given me. Since, then, the children have shared in flesh and blood, he himself likewise became partaker of the same sufferings (Isa 8:18). And how these children were for a sign and a portent to the wisdom of the world and to the pride of the Jews, the same Apostle teaches, who says that the Lord and Savior chose the foolish and weak things of the world, to confound the wise and the strong things (1 Cor 1). Hence the Savior too said to the Apostles: Unless you are converted as one of the children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven (Matt 18:3). And the preacher of the new Gospel becomes a child, who puts off the old man, who is corrupted in the desires of seduction, and puts on the new, who is renewed unto knowledge after the image of the Creator.
