Behold, the Sovereign Lord of hosts will break the little flask in terror, and the lofty of stature will be cut down, and the high will be humbled, and the thickets of the forest will be overturned with iron, and Lebanon with its lofty ones will fall. Some think that this passage is still said of the Assyrian: that when he has been crushed, all the nations round about which lay under his dominion are cut down and humbled, and the densest forest is overturned; by which they would have it that μεταφορικῶς the people and the princes are understood. And that Lebanon too falls with its lofty ones, so that no power at all is left to Assyria. Others, however, would have it that from this place begins the passage concerning Christ: especially since both we and the Circumcision confess that what follows also is written of him. He had told above the name of the child to be born of the Virgin, that he would be called Emmanuel; and afterwards, that the conception of the prophetess's womb would be called hasten, strip the spoils, make haste to plunder (Isa 8:3), and that he himself would be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to both houses of Israel: that his government would be upon his shoulder, and he would be called by six names: wonderful, and counselor, and God, and mighty, and father of the age to come, and prince of peace: and that his empire would be multiplied, and of peace there would be no end. Now, in the prologue of his coming, before it is said that he will be born of the stock of Jesse and David, his passion is shown by the figure of the broken flask: that, by God's will, his flesh was handed over to death for this reason, that the loftiness of the Jews might be destroyed, and those once lofty might fall to the earth; and that Lebanon might be cut down with its cedars, of which we read in Zechariah: Open your gates, O Lebanon, and let fire devour your cedars: howl, fir tree, for the cedar has fallen, because the magnificent have been laid waste (Zech 11:1-2). And that he is said to have been crushed and struck by the Father, this too is evidence: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered (Zech 13:7). And another testimony: For they persecuted him whom you struck (Ps 68 [69]:27). The Hebrew word (פארה) PHURA, which Aquila translated κεραμεῖον, Theodotion and Symmachus rendered ληνὸν, that is, winepress, which itself too, according to the title of three psalms, signifies the Lord's passion, as he himself says in Isaiah: I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was no man with me (Isa 63:3). But the Seventy, bringing in a new sense, translated glorious ones for winepress.

n: Root. Juda shall not be exterminated, like the Assyrians. (Calmet) --- Christ shall spring from the blessed Virgin [Mary], (Worthington) for the salvation of mankind. In him dwelt the fullness of the Spirit; therefore I acknowledge him to be "the rod of the stem of Jesse." His blooming flower shall be my Christ, upon whom has rested, according to Isaiah, "the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and piety, and of the fear of the Lord." Now to no man, except Christ, would this diversity of spiritual proofs suitably apply. HOMILIES ON ISAIAH 3

On this account a "man" is sought who may be with these "seven" spiritual "women", that he may "take away their reproach". Properly there is "one" "man" who may "take away their reproach". Who is this "man"? Jesus, who "came forth according to the flesh" "from the root of Jesse", "made of the seed of David according to the flesh, predestined the Son of God in power according to the spirit of justification". For "there came forth a rod from the root of Jesse". The "rod" is not "the firstborn of all creation", the "rod" is not "he who in the beginning was with God, God the Word", but "a rod from the root of Jesse", who "was born according to the flesh". "There came forth", therefore, "a rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower ascended from his root". What is the "flower" and what is the "root"? For both are one in him who lies beneath; but the difference is one of dealings. For if you are a sinner, there is no "flower" for you, nor will you see the "flower which is from the root of Jesse"; for the "rod" will come even to you, just as the disciple speaks of the "rod" and the "flower". Of the "rod" indeed he says: "what do you wish? shall I come to you with a rod?", but of the "flower": "or in the love of God and the spirit of gentleness?". "There came forth", therefore, "from the root of Jesse a rod" for him who is punished with penalties, a "rod" for him who needs rebuke, a "rod" for him who has need to be reproved; but a "flower" for him who is already instructed and does not need harsh correction, or at least does not need punishments, but is now strong enough to begin to flower toward perfect fruit. For first the "flower" is shown, and then after the "flower" it becomes a "rod" unto fruit. "There came forth a rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower ascended from his root. And the seven women shall rest, the Spirit of God, the spirit of wisdom and understanding shall rest upon him". For the "spirit of wisdom" did "not rest" in Moses, the "spirit of wisdom" did "not rest" in Joshua son of Nun, the "spirit of wisdom" did "not rest" in each of the prophets, in Isaiah, in Jeremiah.

But do not stone me as though I were blaspheming, while I desire to glorify my Lord Jesus Christ; rather, bearing with me, consider what is said, and you will see that in none of them did the "spirit rest", not because it came to none, but because it "rested" in none. It came "upon" Moses, and Moses does not believe after the "spirit of wisdom" that came to him. For he says: "Hear, you rebels: shall I bring forth water for you out of this rock?" It came "upon" all the just, it came also "upon" Isaiah. But what does he say? "Having unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people having unclean lips". The "spirit of wisdom" came after that "tongs" and fire, it came to him "having unclean lips", but it did "not rest". It used him indeed as a minister, but it did "not rest"; it is troubled, to whatever of men it comes. For every man sins, "there is no just man upon the earth who does good and does not sin"; "no one is clean from filth, not even if his life be of one day, but his months are numbered". Therefore it "rests upon" none. We can also prove from the Gospel that the "spirit came upon" many and "did not remain in" them. A little while ago it was read: "my spirit shall not remain in these men forever"; he does not say: it shall not be, but: "it shall not remain". John saw one alone in whom it "remained", and this was the sign: "upon whom you shall see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, this is the Son of God". A certain one ministered to the Word of God when the "spirit descended"; a little after he "sins", a little after he speaks an "idle word". But I do not know whether he even remains without sin; do you think that, with the "spirit" present, it is granted to sin? "Upon" none, therefore, did "the Spirit of God rest", according to what is written: "there came forth a rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower ascended from his root, and the Spirit of God shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom, the spirit of understanding, the spirit of counsel and might". On account of this he is the "angel of great counsel", on account of this he grew strong and, growing strong, ascended, and the powers marvel at him as he ascends and say of him: this is "the Lord strong and mighty in battle". To him, then, as he ascends into the heavenly places, or to his strength, I will say that: "the spirit of counsel and might rested upon him"; "the Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become for me salvation". "There rested", therefore, "upon him the Spirit of God, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and piety, and the spirit of the fear of God filled him".
On the Holy Spirit 2.5

Moreover, he wonderfully expressed his incarnation, saying: From the shoot, my son, you have ascended; in that he sprouted as a plant of the earth in the womb of the Virgin, and as a flower of sweet fragrance, he ascended for the redemption of the whole world, emitted by the maternal womb with the splendor of new light, just as Isaiah says: A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots. And there shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots shall bear fruit. The root is indeed the family of the Jews, the branch is Mary, the flower is Christ of Mary, who when he shines forth in our land and delights the field of the soul, or blossoms in his Church, we cannot fear the cold, nor dread the rain, but await the day of judgment.

And there shall come forth a rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from his root: and the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and godliness: and the spirit of the fear of the Lord shall fill him. Up to the beginning of the Vision, or burden, of Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amos saw, all this prophecy is about Christ, and we wish to explain it part by part, lest, being set forth and discussed all at once, it confuse the reader's memory. The Jews interpret the rod and the flower from the root of Jesse as the Lord himself: namely, that in the rod the power of one who reigns is shown, in the flower his beauty. But let us understand the rod from the root of Jesse as the holy Virgin Mary, who had no shoot clinging to her; of whom we also read above: Behold, a Virgin shall conceive and bear a son (Isa 7:14). And the flower as the Lord Savior, who says in the Song of Songs: I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys (Song 2:1). For root, which the Seventy alone translated, in the Hebrew there is written (גזע) GEZA, which Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion interpreted as κορμὸν, that is, trunk. And for flower, which in Hebrew is called (נצר) NESER, they translated sprout, to show that long after the time of the Babylonian captivity, when no one of David's stock possessed the glory of the ancient kingdom, Mary arose as if from a trunk, and Christ from Mary. That saying in the Gospel of Matthew of which all churchmen seek, and do not find, where it is written, For he shall be called a Nazarene (Matt 2:23), the learned among the Hebrews think was taken from this place. But it must be known that this NESER is written with the letter SADE, whose peculiar quality and sound, between z and s, the Latin tongue does not express. For it is a hissing sound, and is uttered with clenched teeth, barely, by the pressure of the tongue: and with it the city Zion too is written. Further, Nazirites, whom the Seventy translated sanctified, Symmachus separated, are always written with the letter ZAIN (ז).
Commentary on Matthew

And coming he dwelt in a city that is called Nazareth, that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: For he shall be called a nazarene. And it is right that when the creation is restored, all the animals should obey and be in subjection to man, and revert to the food originally given by God (for they had been originally subjected in obedience to Adam), that is, the productions of the earth. But some other occasion, and not the present, is [to be sought] for showing that the lion shall [then] feed on straw. And this indicates the large size and rich quality of the fruits. For if that animal, the lion, feeds upon straw [at that period], of what a quality must the wheat itself be whose straw shall serve as suitable food for lions?

The predicted blessing, therefore, belongs unquestionably to the times of the kingdom, when the righteous shall bear rule upon their rising from the dead; when also the creation, having been renovated and set free, shall fructify with an abundance of all kinds of food, from the dew of heaven, and from the fertility of the earth: as the elders who saw John, the disciple of the Lord, related that they had heard from him how the Lord used to teach in regard to these times, and say: The days will come, in which vines shall grow, each having ten thousand branches, and in each branch ten thousand twigs, and in each true twig ten thousand shoots, and in each one of the shoots ten thousand clusters, and on every one of the clusters ten thousand grapes, and every grape when pressed will give five and twenty metretes of wine. And when any one of the saints shall lay hold of a cluster, another shall cry out, "I am a better cluster, take me; bless the Lord through me." In like manner [the Lord declared] that a grain of wheat would produce ten thousand ears, and that every ear should have ten thousand grains, and every grain would yield ten pounds (quinque bilibres) of clear, pure, fine flour; and that all other fruit-bearing trees, and seeds and grass, would produce in similar proportions (secundum congruentiam iis consequentem); and that all animals feeding [only] on the productions of the earth, should [in those days] become peaceful and harmonious among each other, and be in perfect subjection to man.

And these things are borne witness to in writing by Papias, the hearer of John, and a companion of Polycarp, in his fourth book; for there were five books compiled (συντεταγμένα) by him. And he says in addition, "Now these things are credible to believers." And he says that, "when the traitor Judas did not give credit to them, and put the question, 'How then can things about to bring forth so abundantly be wrought by the Lord.' the Lord declared, 'They who shall come to these [times] shall see.' " When prophesying of these times, therefore, Esaias says: "The wolf also shall feed with the lamb, and the leopard shall take his rest with the kid; the calf also, and the bull, and the lion shall eat together; and a little boy shall lead them. The ox and the bear shall feed together, and their young ones shall agree together; and the lion shall eat straw as well as the ox. And the infant boy shall thrust his hand into the asp's den, into the nest also of the adder's brood; and they shall do no harm, nor have power to hurt anything in my holy mountain." And again he says, in recapitulation, "Wolves and lambs shall then browse together, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox, and the serpent earth as if it were bread; and they shall neither hurt nor annoy anything in my holy mountain, says the Lord." [Isaiah 40:6, etc.] I am quite aware that some persons endeavour to refer these words to the case of savage men, both of different nations and various habits, who come to believe, and when they have believed, act in harmony with the righteous. But although this is [true] now with regard to some men coming from various nations to the harmony of the faith, nevertheless in the resurrection of the just [the words shall also apply] to those animals mentioned. For God is rich in all things. And it is right that when the creation is restored, all the animals should obey and be in subjection to man, and revert to the food originally given by God (for they had been originally subjected in obedience to Adam), that is, the productions of the earth. But some other occasion, and not the present, is [to be sought] for showing that the lion shall [then] feed on straw. And this indicates the large size and rich quality of the fruits. For if that animal, the lion, feeds upon straw [at that period], of what a quality must the wheat itself be whose straw shall serve as suitable food for lions?
HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 10:3

When he saith, "Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;" he is signifying the exaltation of the lowly, the humiliation of the self-willed, the hardness of the law changed into easiness of faith. For it is no longer toils and labors, saith he, but grace, and forgiveness of sins, affording great facility of salvation. Next he states the cause of these things, saying, "All flesh shall see the salvation of God;" no longer Jews and proselytes only, but also all earth and sea, and the whole race of men. Because by "the crooked things" he signified our whole corrupt life, publicans, harlots, robbers, magicians, as many as having been perverted before afterwards walked in the right way: much as He Himself likewise said, "publicans and harlots go into the kingdom of God before you," because they believed. And in other words also again the prophet declared the self-same thing, thus saying, "Then wolves and lambs shall feed together." For like as here by the hills and valleys, he meant that incongruities of character are blended into one and the same evenness of self-restraint, so also there, by the characters of the brute animals indicating the different dispositions of men, he again spoke of their being linked in one and the same harmony of godliness.
HOMILIES CONCERNING THE STATUES 3:5

I have heard many saying, "The threats of a king are like the wrath of a lion;" being full of dejection and lamentation. What then should we say to such? That He who said, "The wolves and the lambs shall feed together; and the leopard shall lie down with the kid, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox," will be able to convert the lion into a mild lamb. Let us therefore supplicate Him; let us send an embassy to Him; and He will doubtless allay the Emperor's wrath, and deliver us from the impending distress.
LETTER 130.8
Not of course that the ox may learn ferocity from the lion but that the lion may learn docility from the ox.
Commentary on Hosea

And I will strike a deal with them in that day, with the beasts of the field and with the birds of the sky and with the creeping things of the ground; and I will shatter from the land, the bow, the sword, and war. And I will cause them to sleep with security. (LXX) And I will make a covenant with them in that day, with the beasts of the field, and with the birds of the sky, and with the creeping things of the earth; and I will break the bow, and the sword, and war out of the land, and I will cause them to dwell in hope. When all the words of the opposing religion have been taken away from the people confessing the Lord, and he calls me, "my husband," and not "Baal," that is, "my idol," then I will strike a deal and agreement with them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky and with the creeping things on the ground. From this time on, Isaiah speaks: "The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the goat. The calf, the lion, and the sheep will live together, and a small child will lead them all. The calf and the bear will graze and their young will rest together. The lion will eat straw like an ox." He desires neither flesh nor blood, but feeds on clean and simple foods. When Peter was instructed to welcome Cornelius among the nations, it was revealed and commanded that he should eat all kinds of animals and recognize nothing as unclean, which he received with thanksgiving. Later, he was told: "What God has cleansed, you must not call common." Therefore, at the coming of the Lord and Savior, after his triumphs in the resurrection, and his ascent to the Father, two walls were joined together by a corner stone, made one by him who made both: and he called her who was called, "Without mercy, mercy obtained": and those who were said, "Not my people," his people: and with all things pacified, the bow and sword shall be brought to nothing, and war shall cease. For there will no longer be a need for weapons of those who fight, when those who fight no more exist. Israel shall be joined to the Gentiles, and that of Deuteronomy shall be fulfilled: "Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people". "God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel."
Commentary on Isaiah

But according to the life-giving spirit, the understanding is easy. For the wolf, Paul, who at first persecuted and tore the Church, of whom it was said: Benjamin a ravening wolf, dwelt with the lamb, either with Ananias, by whom he was baptized (Gen 49:27; Acts 8), or with the apostle Peter, to whom it was said: Feed my lambs (John 21). And the leopard, who formerly did not change his spots, washed in the fountain of the Lord, lay down with the kid, not the one which is on the left, but the one which is sacrificed in the Lord's pasch. And this is to be noted, that it is not the lamb and the kid that dwell and lie down with the wolf and the leopard, but the wolf and the leopard that imitate the innocence of the lamb and the kid. The lion too, formerly most ferocious, and the sheep, and the calf, will abide together. This we see daily in the Church: rich and poor, powerful and lowly, kings and private men abiding together, and being ruled in the Church by little children, whom we understand as the Apostles and apostolic men, unskilled in speech but not in knowledge.
Commentary on Isaiah

The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; the calf and the lion and the sheep shall abide together, and a little child shall drive them. The calf and the bear shall feed: their young ones shall rest together, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. And the infant at the breast shall delight over the hole of the asp; and he that has been weaned shall put his hand into the den of the basilisk. They shall not hurt, and they shall not kill in all my holy mountain, for the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters of the sea that cover it. These things too the Jews, and our judaizers, contend will come to pass according to the letter: that in the glory of Christ, who they think will come at the end of the world, all beasts will be brought back to gentleness, and, laying aside their former fierceness, the wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the rest with the rest, which we now see to be opposed to one another. We must ask them whether, if everything in the present place is taken just as it is written, and nothing is referred to a spiritual understanding, according to the saying of the Apostle: Blessed be God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ (Eph 1:3), then the root and the rod and the flower too are not to be referred to a sense; and the earth struck by the word of God, and the wicked slain by the spirit of his lips, are to be understood just as they are written; and whether they will be forced to teach how the reins of the Lord are girded with incorporeal things, righteousness and truth? But let us ask them this too: what is worthy of the majesty of the Lord in the wolf and the lamb feeding together, and the leopard lying down with the kid, and the lion eating straw, and a little child putting his hand into the hole of asps? Unless perhaps, according to the fables of the poets, they will restore to us the golden age of Saturn, in which wolves and lambs will feed together, and rivers will run full of honeyed wine, and the sweetest honey will drip from the leaves of the trees, and all things will be filled with fountains of milk. But if they answer that these things will come about for the blessedness of the times, so that men may enjoy all good things without harm to anyone, let them hear from us that nothing is good except virtue, and nothing evil except vice, as the Psalmist says: Who is the man who wills life, and loves to see good days? Restrain your tongue from evil, and let your lips not speak guile. Turn aside from evil, and do good (Ps 33 [34]:14; 30 [31]:27). Riches, moreover, and health of body, and abundance of all things, and their opposites, poverty, sickness, and want, are reckoned even among the philosophers of the world neither among goods nor among evils, but are called indifferent. Hence the Stoics too, who agree with our doctrine in very many points, call nothing good but honor and virtue alone, and nothing evil but baseness. We have said these things briefly to convict our judaizers of snoring in the heaviest sleep.
Homilies on Ezekiel, Book 2, Homily 4

For behold, we who seem clothed in religious habit have come together from the diverse condition of the world to faith and to hearing the word of the almighty Lord, and from dissimilar iniquities we have been gathered into the concord of holy Church, so that what is said of the promise of the Church through Isaiah now seems to have been openly fulfilled: "The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid." For through the bowels of holy charity the wolf dwells with the lamb, because those who were plunderers in the world rest in peace with the gentle and meek. And the leopard lies down with the kid, because he who was spotted with the stains of his sins consents to be humbled with him who despises himself and confesses himself a sinner. Where it is also added: "The calf and the lion and the sheep shall dwell together," because he who prepares himself as a daily sacrifice to God through a contrite heart, and another who raged severely from cruelty like a lion, and another who perseveres in the simplicity of his innocence like a sheep, have come together in the folds of holy Church. Behold what charity is like, which kindles, burns up, melts together the diversities of minds and reforms them as it were into one appearance of gold.
The Six Days of Creation, 5.2.6

Such is the grace of the waters, that their calves and lions flee from them, so that this prophetic saying about the sanctity of the Church rightly applies to them: Then wolves and lambs will graze together, and lions and oxen will eat straw together. No wonder, since even in the Church, water works in the same way, that the washed-away wickedness of the thieves is compared with the innocence.
Commentary on Isaiah

And when they have been bound together by the discipline of the Lord, so that their households too are joined, then will be fulfilled: Their young ones shall rest together. The lion too will eat not flesh but straw, namely, he will feed on simple food. And here it must be observed that it is not the ox that eats flesh, but the lion that eats straw. By straw I think the simple words in the holy Scriptures are understood; and by the wheat and the inner marrow, the sense which is found within the letter: and it often happens that men of the world, ignorant of mystical things, are fed on the simple reading of the Scriptures.
Morals on the Book of Job, Book 32, Section 18

If we carefully examine the words of the Prophets, we discover that these and they were put forth by the same Spirit. For when Isaiah observed the life of sinners devoured by the ancient and insatiable enemy, he said, "the lion shall eat straw like the ox." But what is signified by the words hay, and straw, except the life of the carnal? Of which it is said by the Prophet, "All flesh is hay." He then who here is 'Behemoth,' is there a 'lion;' they who are here called 'hay,' are there called 'straw.' But the mind strives to enquire why this lion in Isaiah, or Behemoth as he is called by the voice of the Lord, is in both passages compared not to a horse, but an ox. But we ascertain this the sooner, if we consider what is the difference of foods in the two animals. For horses eat hay, however dirty, but drink clean water only. But oxen drink water, however filthy, but feed only on clean hay. What then is it, for which this Behemoth is compared to an ox, which feeds on clean food, except that which is said of this ancient enemy by another Prophet: "His food is choice." For he rejoices not in seizing those whom he beholds lying of their own accord in the lowest depths with himself, involved in wicked and filthy actions. He therefore seeks to eat hay as an ox, because he seeks to wound with the fang of his suggestion the pure life of the spiritual.
Homilies on Ezekiel, Book 2, Homily 4

Hence there too it is added: "And a little child shall lead them." Who is this little child except he of whom it is written: "A child is born to us, a son is given to us"? He leads those dwelling together, because lest our hearts cling to earthly things, he daily inflames them through inward desire. And this very leading of his is to kindle us unceasingly to love of him, lest when we love one another we remain in mind in this exile, lest the rest of this life so please us that it leads to forgetfulness of our homeland, lest the mind delighted by prosperity grow sluggish.
AGAINST MARCION 4.24

Happily the Creator has promised by Isaiah to give this power even to little children, of putting their hand in the cockatrice den and on the hole of the young asps without at all receiving hurt. And, indeed, we are aware … that under the figure of scorpions and serpents are portended evil spirits, whose very prince is described by the name of serpent, dragon and every other most conspicuous beast in the power of the Creator. This power the Creator conferred first of all upon his Christ, even as the ninetieth psalm says to him: "Upon the asp and the basilisk shall you tread; the lion and the dragon shall you trample under foot." So also Isaiah: "In that day the Lord God shall draw his sacred, great and strong sword" (even his Christ) "against that dragon, that great and tortuous serpent; and he shall slay him in that day."

The infant too, who is a little one in malice, puts his hand into the hole of the asp, and drives demons out of the possessed bodies of men. Hence power was given to the Apostles too to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the strength of the enemy (Luke 10).

And in other words also again the prophet declared the self-same thing, thus saying, "Then wolves and lambs shall feed together." For like as here by the hills and valleys, he meant that incongruities of character are blended into one and the same evenness of self-restraint, so also there, by the characters of the brute animals indicating the different dispositions of men, he again spoke of their being linked in one and the same harmony of godliness. Here also, as before, stating the cause. That cause is, "There shall be He that riseth to reign over the Gentiles, in Him shall the Gentiles trust:" much the same as here too he said, "All flesh shall see the salvation of God," everywhere declaring that the power and knowledge of these our Gospels would be poured out to the ends of the world, converting the human race, from a brutish disposition and a fierce temper to something very gentle and mild.
Commentary on Isaiah

And the animals that were once venomous will in no way be able to hurt and kill those who dwell on the holy mountain of God, which means the Church, of which it is said in the Gospel: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden (Matt 5:14). And lest we think that this is said of mount Zion, according to the error of the Hebrews, in the following verse the mysteries of the Gospel preaching are shown: For the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord: this is what was said more obscurely above: The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and according to their custom the prophetic words are laid open at the end: Like the waters, he says, of the sea that cover. As the waters of the sea cover the depths of the sea, that is, the earth which is covered by the waves, so the whole earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord. This joining together of those who were formerly of diverse ways the blessed apostle Peter too testifies that he saw in the linen vessel (Acts 10) which was let down from heaven, having four corners, which we understand as the four quarters of the world, so that we may recognize the earth filled with the knowledge of God: in which vessel there were four-footed beasts, and serpents, and wild beasts, and birds of heaven, so that what the Ark did in the flood, the Church may do in the world.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 1:6.13-15

Paul testifies to our Redeemer when he says, "He was made a curse for us." The wood of the cross is also announced through the prophet, who said, "The Lord reigned from a tree," and again, "Let us put wood in his bread." But the wood of the cross is explicitly revealed through the gospel, where the prophesied passion of the Lord is described.This very same cross is also maintained in words and works through the apostles, as when Paul writes, "The world is crucified to me and I to the world," and again, "May I glory in nothing except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." For us who strive to reach the eternal homeland, therefore, sacred Scripture is the sea in its four aspects. It announces the cross because it bears us on a tree to the land of the living. Had the prophet not found a likeness between sacred Scripture and the sea, he never would have said, "The earth is full of the knowledge of the Lord, like the waters covering the sea." It follows, then: "The four had one likeness and their appearance and work was like a wheel within a wheel." The four had one likeness because what the law proclaimed, so also did the prophets; and what the prophets announced, the gospel set forth; and what the gospel set forth, the apostles proclaimed throughout the world. The likeness of the four is one, therefore, because even though the divine words are distinct with regard to time, they are nevertheless unified to those who hear them.
"And their appearance and work was like a wheel within a wheel." The wheel within a wheel is the New Testament within the Old, as we have already said, for what the Old Testament signifies, this the New Testament displays. Let me speak succinctly of complex matters. What does it mean that Eve is produced from a sleeping Adam if not that the church is formed from the dying Christ? What does it mean that Isaac bore wood as he was led to be sacrificed and that he continued to live after he had been laid on the altar, if not that our Redeemer himself bore the wood of the cross as he was led along and that he died in sacrifice for us according to his humanity but nevertheless remained immortal in his divinity?
Commentary on Isaiah

In that day the root of Jesse, who stands as a sign of the peoples: him the nations shall beseech, and his sepulcher shall be glorious. LXX: And there shall be in that day the root of Jesse, and he who shall rise up to be prince of the nations; in him the nations shall hope, and his rest shall be honor. For his rest, there is set in the Hebrew MNUATHO (מנחתו), which all translated alike. For honor too there is read in the Hebrew CHABOD (כבוד), which plainly means glory. And the sense is: his death shall be glorious, so that what the Savior prays in the Gospel may be fulfilled: Father, glorify me with the glory which I had with you before the world was (John 17:5). It has been said of his birth, it has been said of the other mysteries in between: he comes to death, which, not by the customary name used of mortals, but because in Christ there was everlasting life, is called rest. But we, to make the sense plain to the reader, for sleep and rest translated sepulcher, another word but the same sense. At that time, then, when the Gospel of Christ has flashed forth in the whole world, and all the earth has been filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters of the sea covering the earth, there shall be the root of Jesse, and he who shall ascend from its stock as a sign of all the peoples, so that the peoples may see the sign of the Son of man in heaven (Matt 24). He will have horns in his hands, in which his strength will be hidden, so that, being lifted up, he may draw all things to himself (Hab 3). Or, as the Seventy translated, he will rise again from the dead, to be prince of all the nations, and all the nations will hope in him. This Jacob too (Gen 49:10) attests in mystical speech concerning the tribe of Judah: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up, and he shall be the expectation of the nations.

Long before this tomb [of Christ] was hewn out by Joseph, its glory was foretold in Isaiah's prediction, "his rest shall be glorious," meaning that the place of the Lord's burial should be held in universal honor.

And it shall be in that day, the Lord will set his hand a second time to possess the remnant of his people, which shall be left from the Assyrians, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Ethiopia, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. And he will lift up a sign to the nations, and will gather the fugitives of Israel, and will collect the dispersed of Judah from the four quarters of the earth: and the jealousy of Ephraim shall be taken away, and the enemies of Judah shall perish. Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not fight against Ephraim. And they shall fly upon the shoulder of the Philistines by the sea, together they shall plunder the sons of the East: Edom and Moab shall be the command of their hand, and the sons of Ammon shall be obedient. In that day, that is, at that time, of which it was said above too, when the root of Jesse has risen as a sign of the peoples, or to rule over the nations, the Lord will set his hand a second time; so that it is not, as our judaizers hold, at the end of the world, when the fullness of the nations has come in, that all Israel will then be saved (Rom 11); but let us understand all these things of the first coming. For we cannot, since one day is spoken of both now and above, refer that one to the first coming and this one to the second: lest through these things which follow, those too which went before should have to be referred to that Christ whom the Jews contend has not yet come but is to come. After the calling of the nations, then, which were once reckoned as the tail, Israel will be reckoned as the tail (above, Isa 10): so that the Lord may set his hand a second time and possess the remnant of his people, concerning which we read above too that not all Israel, but a remnant is to be saved, which shall be left from the Assyrians and from Egypt and from the various nations round about. For first the twelve Apostles, and the seventy, and the hundred and twenty souls, and the five hundred to whom the Lord appeared when they were gathered together, then three thousand and five thousand of the Jews believed in the Lord. James too speaks to the apostle Paul, who was himself also of the remnant: You see, brother, how many thousands of the Jews there are who believe? all these are zealous for the law (Acts 21:20). And in the same volume we read: Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men, from every nation that is under heaven, who all marveled and said: Are not these Galileans, and how have we heard each one his own tongue, in which we were born? Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those who dwell in Mesopotamia and Syria, Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia, and Egypt and Libya, and Cyrene, and sojourners from Rome, Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs, we have heard them speaking in our tongues the great works of God (Acts 2:5ff.). From all these nations, then, the remnant of Israel will be saved through the Apostles. The histories of the Church relate that the Apostles, dispersed through the whole world, preached the Gospel: so that some penetrated to the Persians and the Indians, and Ethiopia stretched out her hands to God, and from beyond the rivers of Ethiopia gifts were brought from there to Christ. And lest he seem to signify only the eastern peoples, he adds the rest too: And from the islands of the sea. By the islands of the sea he signifies the western region, which is enclosed by the circuit of the Ocean.
Commentary on Isaiah

He will lift up, then, the sign of the Cross over all nations, and will first gather the people of Israel from the synagogues of the Jews, so that the Apostles might fulfill the command of the Savior, who had said: Go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt 10:6). Finally Paul too speaks to the unbelievers among the Jews: It was necessary that the word of God be spoken first to you; but since you have rejected it, and judged yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the nations, as the Lord commanded us (Acts 13:46-47). By the four quarters he signifies east and west, south and north, so that through these the calling of the world may be shown.
Commentary on Isaiah

At that time, says Isaiah, Ephraim and Judah, who now, while I prophesy, are at odds with each other in hostile hatred, will in no way be enemies, but according to the prophecy of Ezekiel the two rods will be joined into one rod, and those who were formerly separated will be united in the Church of Christ (Ezek 37), so that they toil with common labor among the nations, and fly upon the shoulder of the Philistines by the sea, that is, first preach to the Palestinians of the coast, and then go by sea with winged course to the other nations. Or, according to the Seventy translators: they will fly in the ships of foreigners, together they will plunder the sea: which we may understand from the example of the one apostle Paul, who through Pamphylia, and Asia, and Macedonia, and Achaia, and various islands and provinces, to Italy too (Acts 28), and, as he himself writes, to Spain, was carried in the ships of foreigners (Rom 15). So Ephraim and Judah, that is, those of the twelve tribes from among the Jews who believed in Christ, will together plunder the East, and will stretch out their hands into Edom and Moab, according to what Christ speaks mystically in the person of David: Into Edom I will stretch out my shoe: foreigners will serve me (Ps 59 [60]:10). For these nations, at the time when Isaiah prophesied, were adversaries of the people of the Jews, and therefore he now says that after the root of Jesse has risen to reign among the nations, and the standard of the Cross has been raised for the salvation of the whole world, then Edom too and Moab and the sons of Ammon, that is, the whole breadth of Arabia, give their hands to the Apostles, and in the places of idolatry churches of Christ are raised up.
Commentary on Zechariah

Of these fishers, who go down to the sea and are in ships, Isaiah too prophesies: They shall fly in the ships of foreigners, and together they shall plunder the sea. For in the churches gathered from the number of the nations the apostles flew through the whole world, to plunder the sea and to carry off the spoils of the dragon who reigned in the sea, and of whom it is written: This sea, great and spacious in its arms; there are creeping things without number, small creatures with great. There the ships shall pass through; this dragon whom you formed to mock him. The sea is broad and spacious for the small and great living creatures that dwell with the dragon, and whose number is beyond count.
